# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 16 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 16 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_016_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 8

**1** After she had finished speaking she asked me, "Is there anything else you want to ask?" I said to her, "Why, lady, is the tower built upon water?" "Because," she said, "your life has been saved and will be saved through water. But the tower has been founded upon the word of the almighty and glorious Name, and it is maintained by the invisible power of the Lord." **2** I answered, "This is a great and marvelous thing, lady. But who are the six young men who are building?" "These," she said, "are the holy angels of God who were the first created, and to whom the Lord delivered all his creation to build up and increase and to govern. Through them, therefore, the building of the tower will be completed." **3** "And the other people who bring the stones?" "These also are holy angels of God, but the six are superior to them. The building will be completed and all will rejoice together around the tower, and will glorify God because the building of the tower has been completed." **4** I asked, "Lady, I wish to know about the stones that were rejected and cast away, and about those thrown far from the tower, and the cracked ones." **5** She replied: "The ones rejected near the tower are those who have sinned and wish to repent. On account of this they have not been thrown far from the tower, because they will be useful for the building if they repent. **6** Those who will repent — if they repent — will be strong for the building and will be fitted into the building, if they repent now while the tower is still being built. For when the tower is finished, there will be no more room, but they shall be rejected." **7** "The cracked ones — these are those who have faith, but also have riches of this world. When tribulation comes, on account of their riches and their business dealings they deny the Lord." I said, "Then, lady, when shall they be useful for the building?" "When," she replied, "their wealth which leads them astray has been cut away, then they will be useful to God. For just as the round stone, unless it is cut and loses something from itself, cannot become square, so also those who are rich in this world cannot be useful to God unless their riches are cut away from them." **8** "Lady," I said, "I want to know about the white round stones that were found not fitting into the building — who are they?" She said: "How long will you be foolish and without understanding, asking about everything and understanding nothing? These are those who have faith but also possess the riches of this age. When tribulation comes, on account of their riches and their transactions they deny their Lord."

---

*EMET note: Vision 3.8 — repeated and expanded summary of the stones typology. The repetition suggests this chapter compiled from parallel sources. The rich are consistently the most problematic category.*
